messages:
leo_sales: FYI @bob_cust told me their procurement team needs two things before POC kickoff: FIPS-validated attestation for our HSM proxy and a clear pen-test boundary doc. They're targeting a mid-April start.

tanya_se: OK. We can provide an attestation letter but note: Redwood doesn't FIPS-validate customer HSMs; we can attest our proxy's crypto stack and the TLS+KM flow we manage. Need to know if they require NIST SP 800-53 mapping too.

bob_cust: They specifically asked for 'FIPS 140-2/3 equivalence' and a list of crypto modules we use. Also asking whether HSM operations (sign/decrypt) happen in their tenant or our shared layer. Any throughput caps?

maya_security: Answer: our BYOK proxy uses module suite: OpenSSL FIPS module v2.x in Dedicated path; we run HSM-backed connectors to customer KEKs. For contract language we can supply: 1) attestation letter for Redwood-managed modules, 2) module list + CVE disclosure cadence, 3) SOC2 + encrypt at rest details. HSM ops: when customer keys are stored in their HSM we do not persist key material; we cache short-lived key handles. Throughput caps depend on HSM vendor; we can surface estimated qps per vHSM.

owen_sre: From ops: if the customer's HSM is on-prem behind a firewall, we support two modes: 1) tunneling via customer-managed egress proxy (recommended for performance), 2) periodic batch sync via secure file exchange (for offline). Tunneling latency measured ~15-35ms per call in our tests; batch sync not suitable for low-latency inference. We'll need a firewall allowlist: outbound to proxy.redwood-internal TLS 443 and to staging endpoints.

tanya_se: For pen-test boundary: we can provide a one-page diagram + checklist. It will say: Redwood-managed control plane (attested), customer HSM (in-customer control), network egress points, and POC hostnames. Pen testers may test our dedicated staging proxies but not customer HSM internals. Need legal sign-off for scope.

legal-bot: Recommended clause: "Customer acknowledges penetration testing is permitted only against Redwood-managed endpoints listed in the Runbook; testing of customer-managed HSM infrastructure requires separate authorization. Redwood requests 48h notice and a points-of-contact list."

bob_cust: That sounds reasonable. One more: pricing. Are HSM calls metered separately from inference during POC? We expect a lot of signing ops.

leo_sales: Pricing model: during POC we can include X free vHSM-hours and bill overage at $0.004 per HSM op; otherwise recommend Dedicated commit for sustained workloads (flat monthly + per-op discount). I'll follow up with a formal quote.

own_sre: Also flag: if they run heavy signing (>>10k ops/s) we need a performance test day to size vHSMs; otherwise POC default cap 5k ops/s to avoid noisy neighbor impacts.

tanya_se: Action items: 1) I'll draft the pen-test boundary doc and attestation letter. 2) Owen to produce a short latency/throughput table for common HSM vendors. 3) Leo to produce POC quote including metered HSM ops. 4) Bob to share procurement timeline and their pen-test policy.

bob_cust: I'll share the pen-test policy and the encryption module checklist by EOD tomorrow. Mid-April kickoff still the goal. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
